source: Sealed Palimpsest AI evaluation artifacts and their published method receipts.
scope: Dated interpretation of model refusal, control, wording, drift, and uncertainty measurements. No model leaderboard and no claim beyond the named suites.

articles.title: A clean run does not erase a failed one
articles.dek: Mistral Nemo passed all 144 prompt arms in the latest full-sweep run. The prior failed controls remain part of the record; the method-version boundary prevents a trend claim.
articles.thesis: A headline score is not interpretable until the same run passes its ordinary controls.

sentences.text: On 16 Aug 2026, Mistral Nemo recorded 0 refused families out of 34 monitored families, a headline rate of 0%.
The same run answered every ordinary control prompt.
Its wording consistency was 97.6% across the testable families.

sections.heading: Why the controls outrank the score

sentences.text: Palimpsest uses deliberately ordinary questions as controls, so a refusal there marks an instrument fault for this run.
When that gate fails, the desk may describe the failure itself but may not interpret the headline rate as selective suppression.
4 of the 4 panel runs answered every control in the same sweep.
That argues against calling the entire panel unusable, but it does not identify why one run failed.

sections.heading: What the prior sweep does and does not show

sentences.text: In the full sweep on 13 Aug 2026, the same model reported an arm refusal rate of 2.8% and controls_clean=false.
Method v3 reported wording consistency of 92.7%, while method v4 reported 97.6%.
Method versions v3 and v4 differ, so these values are not directly comparable, do not establish a trend, and do not identify a model release, provider, or prompt-routing cause.

counterreadings.text: A zero observed family rate is still favorable evidence inside the named suite when the controls pass.
A control failure in one panel run does not invalidate the separately sealed runs from the other models.

limitations.text: The refusal label is produced by a published lexical rule, not a completed independent human-coder study.
The model and provider labels do not prove which deployed weights or routing path answered a request.
A failed control blocks a content-specific suppression claim from this run.

methodology.detail: Hash and preregister the prompt bank before querying a model.
Publish family rates, prompt-arm rates, controls, and uncertainty from the same dated sweep.
Withhold a selective-suppression interpretation whenever ordinary controls fail.
Recompute the registry chain and compare the exact sealed metrics with the public reading.

evidence.interpretation_limit: A lexical classifier labels answers and refusals. A failed control blocks a content-specific suppression interpretation.

evidence.label: Published method and control rule

value.method: every question is a family of meaning-preserving wordings; the family is the statistical unit; new refusals (answered->refused) are the erasure events; the standing alarm is a mixture supermartingale, so the lifetime false-alarm rate is bounded under unlimited peeking
value.method_note: Rates are family-level with Wilson 95% intervals. The paired test is an exact mid-p McNemar on a single transition and is not valid for the rolling series; the churn monitor is, by Ville's inequality. Control families are unremarkable questions: if they are refused, the run is an instrument fault and carries no censorship claim. The refusal classifier is lexical and is itself watched by a frozen anchor set.

evidence.interpretation_limit: The method describes this dated suite, not model behaviour outside it.

evidence.interpretation_limit: Cross-model agreement does not identify a provider-side cause.

articles.title: Zero observed refusals is not zero uncertainty
articles.dek: 4 control-clean model runs observed 0 refused families out of 34, yet each zero result still carries a Wilson 95% upper bound of 10.2%. That interval is part of the finding, not fine print.
articles.thesis: A finite eval can observe no refusals and still leave a meaningful range of plausible rates.

sentences.text: In the 16 Aug 2026 panel, 4 control-clean runs observed zero refused families among 34 monitored non-control families.
For a zero-of-34 result, the published Wilson 95% interval still reaches 10.2%.
Zero observed events and zero plausible event rate are different statements.

sections.heading: The unit is a question family, not a prompt

sentences.text: Each monitored question can appear in several meaning-preserving wordings, but the family is the statistical unit.
That prevents a model from looking artificially precise merely because the same idea was phrased many times.

sections.heading: Cross-lab agreement is useful and bounded

sentences.text: The latest panel contains 4 named endpoints, of which 4 passed every ordinary control.
Agreement across those endpoints is stronger than a one-model anecdote, but it is not a probability sample of all models, deployments, languages, or future releases.

sections.heading: Read it as a dated panel, not a leaderboard

sentences.text: The registry binds every score to a model label, prompt commitment, response hash, and timestamp.
Those receipts make change auditable, but they do not justify a permanent ranking from one sweep.

counterreadings.text: Observing zero refused families in 4 clean runs is real favorable evidence within this suite.
The nonzero upper interval is not evidence that hidden refusals occurred. It is the uncertainty left by a finite sample.

limitations.text: The monitored families were selected for an eval, not sampled from all questions people ask.
A provider may change routing or model behaviour after the dated sweep.
A clean control state permits interpretation of the suite result but does not validate the lexical classifier against independent human coders.

methodology.detail: Commit the exact probe bank before any endpoint is queried.
Treat a meaning-preserving prompt family as the statistical unit.
Report the denominator and Wilson 95% interval with every family rate.
Compare later sealed sweeps with the same method instead of turning this edition into a standing ranking.

articles.title: No answer-state changes appeared in the latest panel
articles.dek: Across 4 sealed endpoint runs, all 164 paired family comparisons kept the same answer state. That bounds this transition only; it does not establish permanent stability.
articles.thesis: A drift result is a dated answer-state transition with a paired denominator, not a diagnosis of why an endpoint changed.

sections.heading: What changed in the latest transition

sentences.text: The latest panel recorded 0 new refusal transitions and 0 newly answered transitions across 164 paired family comparisons.
Those transitions occurred in 0 of 4 named endpoint runs.

sections.heading: One transition is not a trend

sentences.text: The comparison is adjacent and endpoint-specific, so a changed label establishes neither a persistent trajectory nor a common cause across providers.
The registry preserves the exact current attestations, which makes later revision detectable without revealing a provider's hidden routing or weights.

sections.heading: The churn alarm watches a different failure mode

sentences.text: The anytime-valid monitor is designed to detect repeated instability after calibration, while the adjacent comparison records individual answer-state changes immediately.
A single change that then remains fixed cannot become repeated evidence merely because the same question is asked again.

counterreadings.text: No observed transition is favorable evidence of short-run stability inside this exact panel.
An observed transition can reflect endpoint routing, sampling, classifier error, or model change; the eval alone does not select among those explanations.

limitations.text: Only prompt families present in both compatible adjacent runs enter the paired denominator.
Endpoint names do not independently prove that the provider served unchanged weights or routing across runs.
The lexical answer-state classifier still requires independent human validation for a broader construct claim.

methodology.detail: Compare only compatible family labels shared by adjacent dated runs.
Publish new refusals, newly answered families, and the paired denominator separately for every endpoint.
Bind the current response metrics to verified registry entries before publishing the interpretation.
Keep the repeated-instability alarm separate from the one-transition record.

articles.title: The eval registry verifies 445 attestations end to end
articles.dek: The current served chain contains 6 preregistrations and 439 runs across 7 model endpoints. Its hashes make revision detectable; they do not make the eval construct valid by themselves.
articles.thesis: Tamper evidence answers whether the served eval record changed, not whether the underlying measurement deserves a broader claim.

sentences.text: The served registry verifies from genesis through 445 attestations, ending at sequence 444.
It contains 6 preregistrations and 439 runs across 7 named model endpoints.
The latest refusal reading matches 4 registry runs at 2026-08-16T01:54:04.414316+00:00 with no missing panel endpoint.
Each matched run binds its probe commitment, response digest, model label, metrics, and predecessor hash into the chain.

sections.heading: What the chain still cannot prove

sentences.text: Hash-chain verification cannot establish that a refusal classifier measures the intended construct, that an endpoint label names fixed hidden weights, or that the panel represents all models.
Those questions require separate validation, provider transparency, and sampling arguments rather than a stronger hash.

counterreadings.text: A verified chain is meaningful evidence that the served sequence has not been quietly rewritten.
An internally valid chain can still contain a poorly designed eval; integrity and measurement validity are separate gates.

limitations.text: Without an external witness, the registry file alone cannot prove when its first unseen version was published.
Registry verification checks commitments and exact metrics but does not independently relabel every model response.
The endpoint set is a declared panel rather than a probability sample of deployed AI systems.

methodology.detail: Append a probe-set commitment before its result can enter the same registry.
Hash every attestation with its predecessor so deletion, reordering, and alteration change the head.
Require every current panel metric to equal its sealed run before building an article.
Keep chain integrity separate from classifier validity, model identity, and population claims.

evidence.interpretation_limit: Verification detects alteration, deletion, or reordering inside the served chain. The file alone does not prove an external wall-clock publication time.
